chapter.title: What's Changed in ooSQLite 1.1
chapter.para: This chapter lists the changes made in ooSQLite 1.1, compared with ooSQLite 1.0.2.13107, the last version in the ooRexx Subversion repository on SourceForge (incubator/ooSQLite, revision 13111). It is meant both for programmers who use ooSQLite and for the ooRexx community, who may want to review what has been done.

ooSQLite was written by Mark Miesfeld. Its development continues in the GitHub repository JosepMariaBlasco/oosqlite, which contains the complete history imported from Subversion, so that every change described here can be traced to the commit that made it. Each change was made together with a test in the ooSQLite test suite; most bugs were first reproduced by a failing test, and then fixed.

In the rest of the book, the sections that are new in this release are marked &added11; and the sections that changed are marked &changed11;, as the ooRexx reference does. The embedded SQLite is version 3.52.0, as in ooSQLite 1.0.2.13107.

section.title: Changes That Can Affect Existing Programs
section.para: The changes in this section alter the behavior of ooSQLite in a way that an existing program could notice. In every case the old behavior was a bug: it either crashed the process, contradicted the documentation, or silently did something other than what was asked. They are listed first so that they can be reviewed before upgrading.

term.emphasis: Package functions and collations are registered under the name given

listitem.para: When createFunction was given an ooSQLFunction object from a package, or createCollation an ooSQLCollation object, the name argument was ignored: the function or collation was registered under the name it has in the package, and the method still returned OK. SQL that used the given name then failed with "no such function" or "no such collation sequence". For Rexx methods and for library handles the given name was always used.

Now the given name is used in every case. For createFunction, the countArgs argument is also used when it is given; when it is omitted, the number of arguments defined in the package is used, as before. Programs that passed the package name as name, which was the only way for them to work, are not affected. Registering a package with register, loadPackage, or the automatic registration methods still uses the names in the package.

term.emphasis: Removing a user defined function

listitem.para: SQLite identifies a function by its name and its number of arguments. Removing a Rexx function with createFunction(name, .nil) or oosqlCreateFunction(db, name) always asked SQLite to remove the function with 0 arguments, so a function with any other number of arguments stayed in place, while ooSQLite released the memory it used: SQLite was left with a dangling pointer.

Now the number of arguments can be given as the third argument, and then that function is removed. When it is omitted, all the Rexx functions with that name are removed, whatever their number of arguments.

term.emphasis: The authorizer callback gets empty strings, not missing arguments

listitem.para: SQLite passes NULL for the detail strings that do not apply to an action. The authorizer callback of setAuthorizer and oosqlSetAuthorizer did not check for that, so any SQL compiled with an authorizer in place crashed the process. Those arguments are now the empty string, as the documentation of the authorizerCallBack method already said. No working program can depend on the old behavior.

term.emphasis: An aggregate over no rows calls the final method with .nil

listitem.para: For an aggregate over no rows, SQLite calls the final callback without ever calling the step callback, and ooSQLite crashed. Now the final method, or routine, gets .nil as the aggregate object, as the step method does on its first invocation, and decides what the result of an empty aggregate is. See createFunction.

term.emphasis: More errors are reported in lastErrCode and lastErrMsg

listitem.para: The getFunction and getCollation methods of the ooSQLPackage class, and the autoFunction and autoCollation methods of the ooSQLExtensions class, failed for a name the package does not contain without setting the last error: lastErrCode was 0 and lastErrMsg "no error". They now set SQLITE_MISUSE and a message that names the function or collation, like the existing errors for a package that has no functions or collations at all.

term.emphasis: Errors from the final method of an aggregate name that method

listitem.para: When the final method of an aggregate implemented in Rexx returned nothing, or returned something that is not a whole number, the error raised named the step method instead. It now names the final method. Aggregates implemented with routines were not affected.

term.emphasis: Floating point numbers keep their precision

listitem.para: columnDouble of the ooSQLiteStmt class, oosqlColumnDouble, oosqlValueDouble, and the double method of the ooSQLValue class returned the number with 9 significant digits only, whatever the precision of the value: 3.141592653589793 was returned as 3.14159265, and 123456789012.5 as 1.23456789E+11. The conversion of ooRexx used by the native code keeps 9 digits.

Now they return the shortest number, of up to 17 significant digits, that is converted back to the same floating point value: 3.141592653589793 keeps all its digits, 0.1 is still 0.1, and 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004. A program that displays these numbers, or compares them as strings, sees the additional digits. Arithmetic in Rexx is still done with the current NUMERIC DIGITS setting.

term.emphasis: Blob values: an empty blob is not NULL, and the classic routine returns the bytes

listitem.para: In a user defined function, the classic oosqlValueBlob returned a Pointer to the data, which Rexx code could only pass, with its size, to oosqlResultBlob, and .nil for both an empty blob and NULL. The blob method of the ooSQLValue class returned the empty string for both.

Now both return the bytes of the value as a String, the empty string for an empty blob, and .nil for NULL, as the other value routines and methods already did for NULL. Code that passes the result of oosqlValueBlob and its size to oosqlResultBlob keeps working, because oosqlResultBlob accepts a String; code that tested the result for .nil to detect an empty blob must test for the empty string instead.

term.emphasis: oosqlCompileOptionGet counts from 1

listitem.para: oosqlCompileOptionGet passed its index to SQLite unchanged, so the first option was number 0, while the compileOptionGet method of the ooSQLite class, and the column and parameter numbers of the classic interface, count from 1. Now the routine also counts from 1, and returns the same option as the method for every index; 0 returns the string NULL. A loop that starts at 0 and stops at NULL must start at 1, or it lists nothing.

term.emphasis: Mutex objects that can no longer be used raise an error

listitem.para: The enter, leave, and try methods of the ooSQLiteMutex class did nothing on a mutex that had been freed, and try returned OK, as if it had entered it. They now raise the error "The ooSQLite mutex is not valid, it has been closed". Freeing a freed mutex still does nothing.

The mutex objects returned by dbMutex kept using the mutex of their connection after the connection was closed, when SQLite has freed it. They are now closed with the connection, and raise the same error. A program that used them after closing the connection had undefined results before.

term.emphasis: The recordFormat attribute of a statement works

listitem.para: The recordFormat attribute of the ooSQLiteStmt class ran the code of the attribute of the connection on the data of the statement: getting it returned the statement's initCode, normally 0, and setting it changed initCode. It now returns the format given to new, or inherited from the connection, and setting it changes only the format. The attribute of the connection was not affected.

term.emphasis: Canceling all the automatic builtins returns OK

listitem.para: cancelAutoBuiltin with no argument, or with the keyword ALL, returned MISUSE when some builtin extension was not automatic, which was nearly always the case, with the message "Failed to make builtin extension wholeNumber automatic". It now returns OK: afterwards no builtin is automatic, as asked. A single name that is not automatic still returns MISUSE.

term.emphasis: Making automatic what already is does nothing

listitem.para: autoPackage, autoFunction, and autoCollation added the package, function, or collation again when it was already automatic, so that stopping it once left it automatic, and each copy counted against the limit of 10. Marking it again now does nothing.

term.emphasis: Loading a package that is already loaded keeps it

listitem.para: loadPackage of a package that was already loaded made a new package object and replaced the loaded one: getPackage then returned the new object. If the package, or one of its functions or collations, had been made automatic, the automatic registration still used the replaced object, and once it was garbage collected, opening a connection could crash the interpreter. Now the package already loaded is kept: loadPackage applies its dbConn and makeAuto arguments to it and returns true, and getPackage returns the same object as before. A package of the same name from another file, which used to replace the loaded one, is refused: loadPackage returns false, with the new result code OO_PACKAGE_ALREADY_LOADED (1012).

term.emphasis: new of ooSQLPackage and ooSQLLibrary raises an error when it fails

listitem.para: When the library could not be loaded, or was not an ooSQLite package or library, new of the ooSQLPackage class and new of the ooSQLLibrary class returned an object that could not be used, with the error in its lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes, and any other method sent to it crashed the interpreter. They now raise an execution error, 98.900, whose message says what went wrong. new of the ooSQLPackage class also checks the versions of ooSQLite and SQLite that the package requires, as loadPackage did, and raises the error if they are not met; before, it accepted the package. loadPackage and loadLibrary are not affected: they still return false and set the attributes of the ooSQLExtensions class. A package or library made with new is not kept by the ooSQLExtensions class, as before.

section.title: New and Extended Methods and Routines

term.emphasis: The constants of SQLite 3.52.0

listitem.para: The ooSQLiteConstants class had the constants of SQLite 3.8.4.3, the version ooSQLite was written for. The embedded SQLite was updated several times since, but the constants were not, so the extended result codes, open flags, status parameters, limits, and other values added by later versions of SQLite were missing. Following what was done up to SQLite 3.8.4.3, every group of constants of the class now has all the constants of SQLite 3.52.0: 122 new constants, such as CONSTRAINT_ROWID, BUSY_TIMEOUT, OPEN_NOFOLLOW, LIMIT_WORKER_THREADS, or STMTSTATUS_RUN. The constants that SQLite marks as not used or for internal use are left out, as before. Where SQLite renamed a constant, both names are available: for instance MUTEX_STATIC_MAIN and MUTEX_STATIC_MASTER.
DBSTATUS_MAX, the largest connection status parameter, is now 13, the value of SQLite 3.52.0; it was 10.

term.emphasis: ooSQLiteStmt~sql

listitem.para: The new sql method of the ooSQLiteStmt class returns the SQL text of the statement, like the classic oosqlSql routine. Its native code was already in the library, but the class did not define the method.

term.emphasis: New routine oosqlValueInt64

listitem.para: The classic interface had oosqlResultInt64, but not oosqlValueInt64, so a user defined function could not read an argument that does not fit in 32 bits as a whole number. The int64 method of the ooSQLValue class existed. Its native code was already in the library, but under another name, and the routine was not defined.

term.emphasis: ooSQLResult~blob and oosqlResultBlob accept Rexx data

listitem.para: blob of the ooSQLResult class and oosqlResultBlob only accepted a Pointer and a size. The classic oosqlValueBlob returned a Pointer, so the classic interface could pass a blob argument through, but the blob method of the ooSQLValue class returns a String, and Rexx code has no Pointer to its own data: a user defined function written with the object orientated interface could not return a blob at all.
Both now also accept a String, a Buffer, or a MutableBuffer, as bindBlob and oosqlBindBlob do, and the size is then optional. A Pointer and a size are still accepted, so existing code keeps working.

term.emphasis: Result code constants of the extension classes

listitem.para: The ooSQLExtensions and ooSQLPackage classes report errors with the ooSQLite specific result codes 1005 to 1011, which had no constants. They are now constants: OO_NO_CSELF, OO_PACKAGE_NOT_VALID, OO_NO_SUCH_PACKAGE, OO_NO_SUCH_LIBRARY, OO_PACKAGE_NOT_AUTOMATIC, OO_COLLATION_NOT_AUTOMATIC, and OO_FUNCTION_NOT_AUTOMATIC. errStr and oosqlErrStr describe them; they returned "unknown error". A new code, 1012, OO_PACKAGE_ALREADY_LOADED, is described under loadPackage.

section.title: Crashes Fixed
section.para: Each of these bugs crashed the process with a segmentation fault (SIGSEGV). Each one is now covered by a test that reproduced the crash before the fix.

term.emphasis: Loaded libraries and packages and garbage collection

listitem.para: The tables where the ooSQLExtensions class keeps the libraries and packages it has loaded, and the tables where each ooSQLPackage and ooSQLLibrary object keeps its collations and functions, were referenced only from C structures, which the ooRexx garbage collector does not see. Once a collection had run, the next loadPackage, loadLibrary, or getPackage could crash. Any program that loaded a package or a library and kept running for a while was exposed.

term.emphasis: Functions with the same name and a different number of arguments

listitem.para: A function named f with 1 argument and one with 2 arguments are two different functions for SQLite, but ooSQLite kept the data of Rexx functions by name only. Defining the second one released the data of the first one while SQLite still used it.

term.emphasis: Removing a collation needed handler

listitem.para: Calling collationNeeded with .nil, to remove the handler, crashed. The classic oosqlCollationNeeded was not affected.

term.emphasis: The collation needed handler of a package that has none

listitem.para: collationNeeded accepts an ooSQLPackage object and registers the package's handler, but a package does not need to have one; with such a package the method crashed. It now returns MISUSE, as getCollationNeeded already reports an error in that case.

term.emphasis: Metadata of a column declared without a type

listitem.para: tableColumnMetadata and the classic oosqlTableColumnMetadata crashed for a column declared without a type, as a in CREATE TABLE t(a, b TEXT). The data type of such a column is now the empty string.

term.emphasis: The authorizer callback

listitem.para: See above: any SQL compiled with an authorizer in place crashed.

term.emphasis: Aggregates over no rows

listitem.para: See above: an aggregate implemented in Rexx crashed when it was evaluated over no rows.

term.emphasis: Registering a package on a closed connection

listitem.para: register of the ooSQLPackage class crashed with a closed connection, and with an object that is not a connection: in that case it raised the error, but went on. It now raises an error in both cases, as loadPackage does: 98.900 for a closed connection, 88.900 for an object that is not an ooSQLiteConnection.

term.emphasis: Packages and libraries that failed to load

listitem.para: See above: the object that new of the ooSQLPackage or ooSQLLibrary class returned for a library that failed to load crashed the interpreter on its first method. So did an object of a subclass of either class whose init method does not forward to the superclass's; its methods now raise an execution error, 98.900, saying that the object was not initialized.

term.emphasis: Collation and function objects of subclasses

listitem.para: An object of a subclass of ooSQLCollation, ooSQLCollationNeeded, or ooSQLFunction whose init method does not forward to the superclass's crashed the interpreter when it was given to createCollation, collationNeeded, or createFunction. These methods now raise an execution error, 98.900, saying that the object was not initialized.

term.emphasis: Automatic packages after loading them again

listitem.para: See above: loading again a package that was automatic, or whose functions or collations were, could crash the interpreter when a connection was opened.

term.emphasis: oosqlTrace registered a profile routine

listitem.para: The classic oosqlTrace registered its routine as a profile routine: it was called when each statement finished, not when it started, with three arguments, the SQL, a time, and the user data, instead of two, the SQL and the user data; and removing it returned .nil instead of its user data. Programs that took the user data as the third argument of a trace routine must take it as the second one. The trace method was not affected.

term.emphasis: Argument positions in the errors of oosqlExec and oosqlBackupInit

listitem.para: The syntax errors of oosqlExec named the wrong argument: argument 3 for an invalid format, which is argument 4, and argument 4 for a callback routine that does not exist, which is argument 5. oosqlBackupInit named argument 3 for a null source connection, which is argument 2.

term.emphasis: Error messages of routines: handles, arguments, routines

listitem.para: The syntax error 88.900 that the classic routines raise for a null handle called it an object, as in "Argument 1, the mutex object, must not be null.", and for a backup "the backup handle object". The message now says "handle": "Argument 1, the mutex handle, must not be null." Only the text changed; the error code is the same.
In the same way, the errors 88.900 for an invalid option, as in ooSQLiteVersion('X'), said "Method argument" also for routines; they now say "Argument".

term.emphasis: stmtStatus and oosqlStmtStatus with an invalid op

listitem.para: stmtStatus of the ooSQLiteStmt class and the classic oosqlStmtStatus passed their op argument to SQLite unchecked, and SQLite uses it as an index into the array of counters of the statement. An op that was not one of the Status Parameter (stmt) constants returned whatever was in memory past the counters, and with reset true wrote a 0 there, which could corrupt the statement. Such an op now returns 0, and nothing is reset.

term.emphasis: Memory leak in columnIndex and oosqlColumnIndex

listitem.para: columnIndex of the ooSQLiteStmt class and the classic oosqlColumnIndex lost a few bytes of SQLite memory each time they found the column: the upper case copy of its name was never freed. A program that looked up columns by name in a loop kept growing.

term.emphasis: oosqlBackupPageCount and oosqlBackupRemaining

listitem.para: The two routines were crossed twice, in ooSQLite.cls and in the table that registers the native routines; the two errors cancelled out, so they returned the right values. Both places are now correct. There is no change in behavior.

term.emphasis: The example extension libraries

listitem.para: The sample code in examples/user.extensions, which is also used by the test suite, had three bugs, fixed in all the libraries: the ebcdic collation read past the end of equal strings, and crashed when a string was compared with itself; the reverse collation compared only the common part of two strings, so that "ab" and "abc" were equal; and the strAggregate aggregate failed with "out of memory" over no rows, where it now returns NULL, like the group_concat function of SQLite.

term.emphasis: enquote and ooSQLiteEnquote: no length limit, and a stem with one value

listitem.para: ooSQLiteEnquote returned an unpredictable string for a stem with a single value: it built the list in a buffer that was never written in that case. With more values, the list was cut at 4095 characters, and no error was raised when the last value went over. The enquote method of the ooSQLite class had the same limit for arrays of 7 or more items, and none for fewer. Both now return the whole list, whatever its length, and give the same result for the same values. The limit was the size of that buffer, not a limit of SQLite.

term.emphasis: Building with a modern C++ compiler

listitem.para: The register storage class, not allowed in C++17, was removed from ooSQLite and from the example extension libraries.

term.emphasis: Errors of the ooSQLExtensions class

listitem.para: autoCollationNeeded with a package that has no collation needed callback returned false, but the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes said that there was no error: the error was recorded where they do not look. It now sets MISUSE and the message "this package (X) contains no collation needed callback". In the same way, loadPackage refused a package that needs a newer version of ooSQLite or SQLite, but did not say why; it now sets OO_PACKAGE_NOT_VALID, with a message that names both versions.
loadLibrary and resetAutoBuiltin did not reset the last error, so after a successful call the attributes still showed the error of an earlier method.
The message of OO_COLLATION_NOT_AUTOMATIC read "collations X is not an automatically registered collation".

term.emphasis: Package versions are shown as major.minor.level

listitem.para: The message for a package that requires a newer ooSQLite or SQLite showed the versions as internal numbers, "requires ooSQLite version: 6488064 current version: 65536". It now shows them as "99.0.0" and "1.0.0".

term.emphasis: loadExtension resets the last error

listitem.para: When loadExtension loaded the library, it left in the lastErrCode and lastErrMsg attributes the error of an earlier call, such as an earlier loadExtension that had failed. It now sets them to OK and No error, as exec does. Only programs that read the attributes after a successful call see a difference.

The syntax diagrams are now railroad diagrams generated from EBNF, like the ones of the ooRexx reference, instead of text. How to Read the Syntax Diagrams is the common section of the ooRexx books. The diagrams of the methods and routines that were still templates show their real arguments, taken from the code.

The chapter on the ooSQLiteStmt class is now complete: every method and attribute has its arguments, return value, remarks, and, for most of them, a tested example. The method table lists all of them. The example of lastErrMsg displayed the initCode attribute as the error code. The template section of the value method, an internal debugging aid, was removed.

The routines of the classic interface that work on prepared statements are now documented: the oosqlBind and oosqlColumn routines, oosqlStep, oosqlReset, oosqlFinalize, and the others, each one with a link to the equivalent method of the ooSQLiteStmt class, and most of them with a tested example. A new section, Prepared Statements, describes how a statement handle is used, and what happens when a handle that is null, or that has been finalized, is used. The examples of oosqlPrepare and oosqlColumnIndex could not run: they invoked methods on the handles. The routine table of the classic interface lists all the routines; it stopped at oosqlFinalize.

The routines of the classic interface that work on a database connection are documented: oosqlExec, with its result set formats and its callback routine, oosqlClose, oosqlErrCode, oosqlErrMsg, oosqlNextStmt, oosqlLoadExtension, and the others, most of them with a tested example. oosqlLoadExtension and ooSQLiteRegisterBuiltin describe where they leave the error message of SQLite, which is not recorded in the connection: .routineErrorMessage. The section of nextStmt said that a finalized statement could be the starting point of the search; the search then starts from the beginning.

The classic routines that register callback routines are documented: oosqlCommitHook, oosqlRollbackHook, oosqlUpdateHook, oosqlTrace, oosqlProfile, oosqlProgressHandler, oosqlBusyHandler, oosqlSetAuthorizer, oosqlCreateCollation, and oosqlCollationNeeded, each one with the arguments its routine receives and a tested example. A new section, Callback Routines, gives the rules common to all of them: in particular, the routine must be a public routine of the calling program; those of the packages it requires are not found.

The routines of the classic interface used inside user defined functions are now documented: the oosqlResult routines, which set the result of the function, such as oosqlResultInt and oosqlResultError, and the oosqlValue routines, which read its arguments, such as oosqlValueText and oosqlValueType, each one with a tested example. The remarks of oosqlResultBlob and oosqlValueBlob give the rules common to each group. oosqlValueNumericType converts a text to a number in place, which changes what the other routines see afterwards.
The mutex routines of the classic interface are now documented: oosqlMutexAlloc, oosqlMutexEnter, oosqlMutexTry, oosqlMutexLeave, and oosqlMutexFree, with examples that use several Rexx threads.

The classic routines that query the library are now documented: the versions (oosqlLibVersion and others), the compile options, oosqlComplete, oosqlStrGlob, which returns 0 for a match, and the memory routines. The section of oosqlLibVersion notes that .ooSQLite~VERSION invokes the version method of the ooSQLite class, which hides the VERSION constant: the constant is .ooSQLiteConstants~VERSION.

The automatic extension routines of the classic interface are now documented: oosqlAutoExtension, oosqlCancelAutoExtension, and oosqlResetAutoExtension. oosqlCancelAutoExtension was documented under the name oosqlCancelAutoBuiltin, a routine that does not exist.

ooSQLiteMerge and ooSQLiteVersion are now documented, and so is ooSQLiteEncryptionAvailable, a routine that was in ooSQLite but not in the book. With them, every routine of the classic interface has its arguments, return value, remarks, and an example.

The chapters on the ooSQLResult and ooSQLValue classes are now complete: each method has its section, with an example of a user defined function, and the method tables list all of them. Before, only the blob method of ooSQLResult was documented.
The chapter on the ooSQLiteMutex class is now complete, with examples that use several Rexx threads.

The chapters on the ooSQLExtensions and ooSQLPackage classes are now written, with an introduction to the three kinds of native extensions, and examples that use the example libraries of ooSQLite. They say what the names of packages and libraries are, which differ from the names of their files, what is registered automatically and when, and the errors of each method. The table of the User Defined Extension Classes chapter describes each class.

The chapter on the ooSQLLibrary class is now written: it was a copy of the template of another class. It documents the getHandle method, which was missing, and both new methods (of ooSQLLibrary and of ooSQLPackage), which the manual said could not be used from Rexx code.

The chapter on the ooSQLite class was rewritten, with tested examples. It now documents the strGlob and encryptionAvailable methods and the zeroPointer attribute, which were in ooSQLite but not in the book. Its text said that libVersion should match .ooSQLite~VERSION, but that invokes the version method: the constant is .ooSQLiteConstants~VERSION.

The constants chapter lists all the constants of the class, also the ones that were missing from it, such as NOTICE and WARNING. The values of the version constants are those of the embedded SQLite, and the NULL datatype is listed with its ooSQLite name, SQLNULL.

Arguments named after the C++ code were renamed, in the diagrams and in the text: column instead of col and columnName instead of colName in the column methods of the ooSQLiteStmt class and in the classic oosqlColumn routines, and op instead of param in stmtStatus and oosqlStmtStatus, as in SQLite. In the same way, the status parameter is op in status, dbStatus, oosqlStatus, and oosqlDbStatus, and the column is columnName in tableColumnMetadata and oosqlTableColumnMetadata, whose section showed it with no name, and gave the COLLATIONSEQUENCE index misspelled. The classic oosqlStatus, oosqlDbStatus and oosqlTableColumnMetadata routines are now documented.
New section for a method that was not documented: collationNeeded of the ooSQLiteConnection class, with its callback method.
New or rewritten sections: createFunction, oosqlCreateFunction, createCollation, blob of the ooSQLResult class, and oosqlResultBlob.

Diagrams corrected: the count argument of oosqlBackupStep is optional; the user data argument of execCallBack is only present when exec was given one; traceCallBack was shown with the name of another method; attributes show a set form only when they can be set. The text of busyCallBack said that the user data argument was omitted when none was given; it is the .nil object.

The loadExtension and enableLoadExtension methods of the ooSQLiteConnection class are documented, with a tested example; they were missing from the book and from its method table. The example of execCallBack named the default record format OO_OO_ARRAY_OF_DIRECTORIES; it is OO_ARRAY_OF_DIRECTORIES.
The Rexx examples are highlighted, and errors in some of them were fixed, for example in the example of busyHandler.

The chapters of the ooSQLCollation, ooSQLCollationNeeded, and ooSQLFunction classes, which were templates, are written: what the objects represent, where they come from, where they are used, and why programs do not create them, with tested examples. The return value of interrupt is documented. No section of the book is a template any more.

ooSQLite builds on Linux from a clone of the repository with make -f Makefile.lin, which was fixed to work outside the ooRexx build tree. The library needs the variant of APICommon from the ooRexx Subversion repository (incubator/APICommon), now included in the source tree.

The repository contains a test suite of more than 400 tests, written with ooRexxUnit, the framework of the ooRexx test suite. It covers the object orientated and the classic interfaces, the callbacks, the builtin extensions, and the loading of extension libraries and packages, with the test libraries in examples/user.extensions.
Every change is built and tested by continuous integration on Linux.
